chs.t: Principles of the Science of Tajweed

items.t: Its name: It is called the Science of Tajweed and it is related to the knowledge of the makhaarij1 of the Arabic letters and their characteristics2. 2- Definition of Tajweed: Linguistic definition: The word literally means betterment, mastering something and doing it well.

Technical definition: Articulating every letter from its precise makhraj and giving each letter its ‘rights’ in inherent characteristics and ‘dues’ in conditional characteristics.3 3- Its setting: Tajweed is applied to the text of the Noble Qur’an. Some added the words of the Qur’an and the hadith while others said the letters of the Arabic alphabet.
4- Its precedence: It is one of the most honored religious sciences because it is connected to the Book of Allah .

See the glossary. i.e., manner of articulation and phonetic features. The ‘rights’ of a letter are its inherent distinctive qualities such as,,,,, etc. The ‘dues’ of a letter are its conditional characteristics or sound variants [that appear at times and are absent at other times according to its phonetic environment] such as:
,, and  Tafkheem and tarqeeq in (), ( )and (). Details will be discussed later.

5- Its purpose and benefits: The purpose of learning Tajweed is to avoid making mistakes while reciting the Book of Allah, and its fruit is achieving happiness in this life and in the hereafter. 6- Its place within the sciences:

It is one of the religious sciences that are related to the Qur’an. 7- Its founder: When it comes to the practical application, the founder of Tajweed is Prophet Muhammad  who received the Qur’an from Allah through the trustworthy angel Jibreel  with Tajweed rules applied to it.4 Then the Sahabah5 (may Allah be pleased with them) received it from the Prophet  in this way and passed it on to the Taabi‘een6 and so on until it reached us through our teachers in authentic verified chains that are mutawaatir.7 When it comes to the technical and theoretical knowledge, there is a lack of consensus about the founder of Tajweed. Among the possible names are: AbulAswad Ad-Du’ali, Al-Khaleel ibn Aḥmad, Abu-‘Ubayd Al-Qaasim ibn Sallaam, Abu-Muzaaḥim Al-Khaaqaani and other scholars of language and recitations.

8- Its derivation: It is derived from the oral recitation of the Qur’an by the Messenger of Allah , which has reached us from our teachers through mutawaatir chains. The Quran is the verbatim word of Allah  according to Surat Al-Furqaan (25:32).

9- Its technical issues: Examples of its technical issues and rules are: every vowelless ( nūn saakinah) followed by a throat letter should be pronounced clearly from its articulation point without an extra ghunnah; any letter of madd followed by a hamzah in the same word should be prolonged four or five moras (counts), etc.

10- Its ruling: The knowledge of this science is a collective duty ()8 while the general application9 of its rules [which will prevent making major mistakes when reciting the Qur’an] is an individual duty ( )upon every legally responsible Muslim, male and female, who recites the Qur’an.
The Pillars of Tajweed
The four pillars of Tajweed are:
1- Knowledge of the makhaarij of the letters,11

2- Knowledge of the characteristics of the letters, 3- Exercising the tongue by a lot of repetition, 4- Learning the Qur’an orally from expert reciters (i.e., teachers) who have mastered the recitation.

This is an obligation upon the Muslim Ummah as a whole. If some perform it, the rest of the community are relieved from individual responsibility for it. l What is an individual duty ( )is the general application of the rules since the particulars of Tajweed, though highly recommended, are not obligatory.

When it comes to the speed of recitation, there are three levels:12 1- Tarteel : It is reciting the Qur’an slowly and with tranquility while pondering the meanings, articulating every letter from its precise makhraj and giving each letter its ‘rights’ in inherent characteristics and ‘dues’ in conditional characteristics.

2- Ḥadr : It is the fast recitation while observing the rules of Tajweed. 3- Tadweer : It is reciting the Qur’an at a level in between tarteel and ḥadr. These three levels are all permissible. The word in and covers them all.

Some scholars mentioned a fourth level called Tahqeeq that is slower and more tranquil than Tarteel. With this level, one should be careful not to stretch letters, extend any sound longer than its required length or exaggerate the ghunnah. This level is used for learning in a classroom context.
Definition of laḥn : Laḥn is a mistake and deviation from correctness. It is divided into two types: 1- Clear laḥn I13
2- Hidden laḥn I14
Definition of the clear laḥn: It is a mistake that occurs in the pronunciation of a word and clearly disrupts it, whether the meaning of the word is changed or not.

To be considered a clear laḥn, the mispronunciation of a word in a recitation should not be correct according to another mutawaatir recitation or riwayah. Though not a clear laḥn, this kind of error is not permissible since one should not confuse between qira’aat. Examples of such errors:

Why is it called hidden laḥn? It is called hidden laḥn because only those who have knowledge of Tajweed can detect it. Ruling of the clear laḥn: It is forbidden (haraam) and the reciter is sinful if such mistakes are made on purpose.
Ruling of the hidden laḥn: It is disliked (makrūh). Qur’an teachers and reciters consider recitations with hidden laḥn to be flawed.

Definition of isti‘aadhah: Isti‘aadhah is seeking refuge in Almighty Allah and asking for His protection against the accursed Satan. The version agreed upon is: The ruling of saying isti‘aadhah before reciting the Qur’an:

The majority of scholars say it is recommended and some say it is obligatory. Definition of basmalah: Basmalah is the gerund from basmal which means to say: The ruling of saying basmalah at the beginning of surahs: It is a customary obligation to say the basmalah at the beginning of surahs with the exception of Surat At-Tawbah (also known as Surat Baraa’ah).

Options of saying isti‘aadhah and basmalah at the beginning of a surah: There are four options that are all permissible: 1- Separating all of them (Stop-Stop) by stopping to breathe in after isti‘aadhah and then after basmalah; The difference between a religious obligation and a customary obligation is that not fulfilling the religious obligation results in punishment unlike the customary obligation. Nevertheless, it is necessary for a Qur’an reciter to say the basmalah.

2- Separating the first and joining the second to the third (Stop-Connect) by stopping to breathe in after isti‘aadhah, then joining basmalah to the first verse; 3- Joining the first to the second and separating the second from the third (Connect-Stop) by joining isti‘aadhah to basmalah, then stopping to
breathe in; 4- Joining all of them (Connect-Connect) by joining isti‘aadhah to basmalah and then joining the latter to the beginning of the surah.
Options of saying basmalah between two surahs:

items.h: There are four options, but only three are

items.t: permissible: 1- Stopping to breathe in after the last verse of the first surah and again after basmalah;
2- Joining all of them; 3- Stopping to breathe in after the last verse of the first surah, then joining basmalah to the beginning of the second surah.

4- The fourth option that is not permissible: Joining the last verse of the first surah to the basmalah, then stopping to breathe in before starting the first verse of the next surah. It is not permissible because the basmalah comes at the beginning, not at the end of surahs; and it could confuse listeners who might think that the basmalah is the last verse or part of the last verse of the first surah.
Surat Baraa’ah (At-Tawbah) is an exception. Since there is no basmalah at the beginning, there are only two options: 1- Separating isti‘aadhah from the first verse, 2- Joining them.

Surat At-Tawbah is an exception because it does not have the basmalah. It has three three options:20 1- Stopping to breathe in after reciting the last verse of the Surat Al-Anfaal and then starting the first verse of Surat At-Tawbah; 2- Joining the end of Surat of Al-Anfaal to the beginning of Surat At-Tawbah;
3- Joining them while observing sakt.

Options of starting the recitation anywhere in the middle of a surah: When starting the recitation in the middle of a surah, the reciter has the option of saying the basmalah after isti‘aadhah or leaving it out. If he

These three options apply to any surah that precedes Surat At-Tawbah in the musḥaf (not just AlAnfaal). On the other hand, if the surah recited before Surat At-Tawbah follows it in the sequence of the musḥaf, or if Surat At-Tawbah itself was repeated, the only permissible way is to stop at the end of the surah to breathe in before resuming the recitation.
It is necessary to say the basmalah if the reciter starts with words as in the following examples:
To him [alone] is attributed knowledge of the Hour. (41:47)

And with Him are the keys of the unseen. (6:59) This is because if the reciter joins isti‘aadhah to the verse, the meaning becomes very ugly since the pronoun at the beginning of the verse will look as if it refers to Satan. For the same reason, the reciter should not join the basmalah to the verse if he starts with words such as:
Satan threatens you with poverty. (2:268)
Allah cursed him. (4:118)
says basmalah, then he can choose from the above-mentioned four permissible ways. If he leaves the basmalah out, then there are two permissible options: 1- Stopping to breathe in after isti‘aadhah;
2- Joining isti‘aadhah to the verse.
When starting the recitation anywhere in the middle of Surat Baraa’ah, some scholars say that it is permissible to say the basmalah (after Isti’aathah) while others do not allow it.

In Tajweed, the most important areas of study are the makhaarij as well as the phonetic characteristics of the letters that will be discussed later. Indeed, all or most of the technical issues of Tajweed are linked to these two areas. Therefore, it is important to master both of them.

Definition of makhraj : Linguistic definition: The word literally means a place of exit. Technical definition: It is the place where the sound of the letter is emitted and becomes distinctive from other letters. Definition of ḥarf :
Linguistic definition: The word literally means tip. Technical definition: It is a sound emitted from a specific makhraj or an estimated one. How many letters are there in the Arabic alphabet?24

To pinpoint the makhraj of a letter, pronounce the letter with a sukūn or shaddah, preceding it by a voweled hamzah. The makhraj is where the sound ends. The precise makhraj ( )is a specific part of the throat, tongue or lips. This is different from the estimated makhraj ( )such as the hollow space in the mouth and throat ( )where the sound of the letter is not emitted from a specific part.

There are two groups of Arabic letters: original letters and derived letters. The original letters are those that are emitted from a single makhraj while the derived letters are those that originate from two letters or are emitted from two articulation points or makhaarij such as the facilitated hamzah, the voiced that sounds like a heavy and the alif with imaalah.
Some consider the hamzah and the alif to be the same letter, making the total number 28 letters.
How many makhaarij are there?

The Arabic letters have seventeen makhaarij according to the chosen opinion today. How many main sections of the vocal tract are there? The seventeen makhaarij are located in five main sections of the vocal tract. These five sections are the hollow space in the mouth and throat, the throat/pharynx, the tongue, the lips and the nasal cavity .

There is no consensus among Tajweed and language scholars regarding the number of makhaarij and their different schools of thought are as follows:  Al-Khaleel ibn Aḥmad ( teacher of Sibawayh) and those who followed him such as Ibn Al-Jazari specified seventeen makhaarij located in five main sections of the vocal tract.

 Sibawayh and those who followed him such as Al-Shatibi specified sixteen makhaarij located in four main sections of the vocal tract. Sibawayh did not consider the hollow space in the mouth and throat ( )to be a makhraj. Instead, he indicated that the alif is emitted from the same makhraj as the hamzah at the back of the throat, the vowel from the middle the tongue, and the vowel from the lips same as the non-vowel . This used to be the opinion of the majority of Tajweed and language scholars before Ibn Al-Jazari.

 Al-Farra’, Al-Jarmi, Qutrub and those who followed them in this regard specified fourteen makhaarij. They dropped the makhraj of the hollow space in the mouth and throat ( )like the previous school of thought and indicated that the, and are emitted from one makhraj which is the tip of the tongue.
These main sections ( )are sometimes called the general makhaarij ( )as well as the types of makhaarij ().

Definition of madd:
Linguistic definition: increase. Technical definition: It is stretching the voice when articulating a letter of madd or leen.

items.h: What are the letters of madd?

items.t: There are three letters of madd, all of which appear in the word : 1- The alif saakinah that is always preceded by a fatḥah, 2- The saakinah that is preceded by a ḍummah, 3- The saakinah that is preceded by a kasrah. There are two main divisions of Madd:
1- Original madd 2- Derived madd .
The word in Surat Nūḥ means ‘to increase’: And give you increase in wealth and children. (71:12)

The letters and are also leen letters if they have a sukūn and are preceded by a fatḥah on the letter before them. In case of a stop, when followed by a saakin (vowelless) letter in the final position, they become stretched and are treated as the letters of madd. This madd is called .
The Arabic word means ‘branch’. This madd is called because it is an offshoot of the original madd.

The Original Madd Definition of the original madd: It is the normal or natural madd without which the correct pronunciation of the letter would not be realized. There is no cause for this madd other than the presence of one of the madd letters in a given word.
Its regulator:138 No hamzah or sukūn should follow the madd letter.
Its length is equal to that of one alif, i.e., two moras in connected speech and in case of a stop. The length of a mora is the time taken to stretch one’s finger or bend it in a moderate manner.

Definition of the derived madd: It is the madd that is prolonged beyond the normal duration and there is a cause for it. Its regulator: There should be a hamzah or sukūn following the madd letter. What causes the extra length in the derived madd?
Two causes: hamzah or sukūn.

It is described as ‘natural’ because a well-balanced speaker would apply it without any increase or decrease in its timing. It is also called shortening ( )and intrinsic madd (). Or condition. This cannot be precisely measured.

What are its categories? There are many opinions, but in this book we mentioned five categories: the connected madd, the separated madd, the substitute madd, the madd subject to sukūn and the compulsory madd .
Definition of the obligatory connected madd: In this madd a hamzah follows the madd letter within one word. Examples:, and .
It is called so because the hamzah is connected to the madd letter in the same word.
It is called so because it is obligatory according to all qira’aat reciters to make its length exceed that of the natural madd.

If the hamzah precedes the madd letter, this is called substitute madd such as . If the hamzah follows the madd letter within one word, this is the connected madd such as whereas if it follows it in a separate word, this is the separated madd such as and . Sukūn can only follow the madd letter; so if it is a permanent sukūn in connected speech and in case of a stop, this is the compulsory madd such as and if the sukūn is applied only in case of a stop, this is the madd subject to sukūn such as .

What is its length? Its length is four or five moras according to the recitation of Hafs on the authority of ‘Aasim by the way of Ash-Shaatibiyyah. It is permissible to prolong its length to six moras in case of a stop if the hamzah is in the final position such as in .
II. The Permissible Separated Madd Definition of the permissible separated madd: In this madd a hamzah follows the madd letter in a separate word. Examples:, and .
It is called so because the hamzah is separated from the madd letter.
It is called so because there is no consensus among the qira’aat reciters regarding its length. Some prolonged its length two moras while others prolonged it more than that.

The separation between the madd letter and the hamzah may appear in writing such as and it may not. The vocative and the for calling attention are separate words from what follows them but they are written according to the Uthmaani orthography as one word. If followed by a hamzah such as and, the rule of the permissible separated madd is applied since these are in effect two words.
What is its length? Its length is four or five moras according to the recitation of Hafs on the authority of ‘Aasim by the way of Ash-Shaatibiyyah.
Definition of the substitute madd: In this madd the hamzah precedes the madd letter. Examples:, and .
It is called so because the madd letter substitutes a hamzah.
Its length is two moras according to all the qira’aat reciters.

However, there are cases where a hamzah precedes a madd letter but this letter is original and not really a substitute of a hamzah

saakinah such as in the words, and . This is why the substitute madd is also called ‘madd preceded by hamzah’ ( )and this term is more general and comprehensive. Except according to the recitation of Warsh who applied three options: two, four and six moras.

IV. The Madd Subject to Sukūn Definition of the the madd subject to sukūn: In this madd there is a temporary sukūn following the letter of madd or leen in case of a stop ( )but not in connected speech (). Examples:,,,, and .
Why is it called the madd subject to sukūn? It is called so because the madd or leen letter is prolonged only if there is a temporary sukūn following it in case of a stop.

Three lengths are permissible: six, four or two moras (). Holding the madd letter for six moras ( )has precedence over the other options, followed by four moras (). If, however, the letter is a leen letter, then this order is reversed: two, then four and finally six moras.
V. The Compulsory Madd Definition of the compulsory madd:
In this madd there is a permanent sukūn following the madd letter in connected speech ( )and in case of a stop (). Examples:, and when applying the option of replacement ().
In case of a stop, the final short vowel is omitted resulting in a temporary sukūn.

Why is it called ‘compulsory’ (?) It is called so because its cause, which is the sukūn, never parts with it whether in connected speech or in case of a stop. Another reason for being called ‘compulsory’ could be because its consistent prolongation is obligatory.
What is its length?
Its length is always six moras ( )according to all the qira’aat reciters.

chs.t: Al-Waqf: Recitation Pauses in the Qur’an

items.t: Definition of waqf :190 Linguistic definition: stopping, holding back. Technical definition: It is cutting off the sound with the airflow at the end of a word. If the final letter is mutaḥarik, the vowel is replaced by a sukūn. This pause lasts for the usual period of time needed to breathe in with the intention of resuming the recitation.
What is ? Linguistic definition: cutting, separating. Technical definition: It is to stop reciting straight away with the intention of ending the recitation.

Technical definition: Sakt is a breathless pause that cuts off the sound at the end of a word for a period of time less than the usual waqf, estimated by some to be around two moras in length but first and foremost it is learned orally from teachers. Knowing the proper places to begin and to stop during Qur’an recitation ( )is of extreme importance for the reciter. Imam Ali () said that the word tarteel in refers to the tajweed of letters and having knowledge of stops.

This can only be at the end of a verse. If the reciter changes his/her mind and decides to resume the recitation, then Isti‘aadhah is recommended. It was said that the three words, and were synonymous, i.e., having the same meaning.
Areas of Study Related to Waqf
There are three areas:
1- The state of the reciter,
2- The place of stopping,
3- Ways of stopping.
I. Waqf in Relation to the State of the Reciter When it comes to the state of the reciter, there are four categories: 1- Voluntary
2- Waiting
3- Forced
4- Testing

Voluntary waqf: Voluntary waqf is intentional stopping, i.e., the reciter chooses to stop without being affected by any external factor. Waiting waqf: Waiting waqf is for those reciters who combine multiple qira’aat. The reciter stops at the end of a word in order to add the other varients before resuming the recitation.
Forced waqf: This is when the reciter is compelled to stop due to shortness of breath, inability, forgetfulness, etc. Testing waqf: This is when stopping is for examination or education purposes.
II. Waqf in Relation to the Place of Stopping When it comes to the place of stopping, there are four categories:194 1- complete
2- sufficient
3- ḥasan (good)
4- bad i

Complete waqf: Waqf is complete when one stops at the end of words that are not connected grammatically or in meaning to what follows them, such as stopping at the end of surahs, stories or when moving from one topic to another.
Example: Stopping after the word in the following verses:

Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful. Indeed, those who disbelieve – it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them – they will not believe. (2:5-6) Sufficient waqf:

Waqf is sufficient when one stops at the end of words that are linked to what follows them in meaning but not grammatically. Example: Stopping after the word in the following verse: This is only in voluntary waqf. Scholars and Qur’an reciters do not agree about the number of these categories. Some say there are five, four or three categories and some use the term ‘levels’ instead of ‘categories’. Though scholars use different terms, there is no dispute between them.

The bad waqf is mentioned as one of the categories in order to be avoided. When omitted, three categories will be left as Ibn Al-Jazari mentioned in his poem: “( ”three: complete, sufficient and good).

Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful. Ḥasan (good) waqf: Waqf is ḥasan when one stops at the end of words that are connected to what follows them grammatically and in meaning but the words have a correct meaning on their own.
Example: Stopping after in Surat Al-Faatiḥah:
[All] praise is [due] to Allah, Lord of the worlds. (1:2) Bad waqf:

Bad waqf is when one stops at the end of a word or phrase that does not convey a complete thought or gives a distorted meaning. Examples of waqf at words that do not convey a complete thought: Stopping after in or after in .
Examples of waqf at the end of words that give distorted meanings: - Stopping after the word in the following:
Indeed, Allah is not timid to present an example - that of a mosquito or what is smaller than it. (2:26) - Stopping after the word in the following:
Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people. (63:6)
i.e, the sentence is incomplete and the meaning is not understood.
- Stopping after the word in the following:

O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying. (4:43) What are the rulings of these four categories of waqf? Ruling of the complete and the sufficient waqf: It is fine to stop at the end of words that fall under either of these categories and then resume the recitation starting with that which follows.

Ruling of the ḥasan waqf: It is fine to stop at the end of words that fall under this category and then resume the recitation starting with that which follows if this occurs at the end of a verse such as stopping after . This is called the permissible ḥasan waqf because it is permissible to start with what follows. However, if this does not occur at the end of a verse such as stopping after in, it is still fine whether the waqf is voluntary or forced, but one should not resume the recitation starting from the word that follows.
Instead, one should go back and repeat the last word or words depending on the meaning.

Ruling of the bad waqf: It is not permissible to stop at the end of words that fall under this category except if one is compelled (forced waqf). When resuming the recitation, one should go back and repeat the last word or words.

items.h: III. Waqf in Relation to Ways of Stopping

items.t: When it comes to ways of stopping, there are three categories: 1- Iskaan
2- Ishmam
3- Rawm

What is waqf with iskaan? It is the omission of the final short vowel, replacing it with a pure sukūn. Which vowel diacritical marks can iskaan be applied to? Iskaan can be applied to all vowel diactitical marks.

What is waqf with ishmam? It is the rounding of the lips as when pronouncing a ḍummah immediately after applying iskaan to the final letter of the word without producing any sound since it is to be seen but not heard.
Note:

There is no waqf in the Qur’an which is compulsory (if skipped, the reciter is considered a sinner) or forbidden (if made, the reciter is considered a sinner) except that which has a reason. For example, it is forbidden to stop on purpose after which means ‘there is no god’ or to start on purpose from which means ‘indeed Allah is poor’ even if the reciter does not want to convey these meanings. If there is intention to convey these meanings, then this person has become a disbeliever.

This takes place whether the word is built on one form (fatḥah, ḍummah or kasrah) or conjugated, i.e., the last mark changes according to its grammatical position in the sentence. Indicating the vowel diacritical mark of the final letter, i.e., the ḍummah.

When can ishmam be applied? It can only be applied when the final letter of a word has a ḍummah, whether the word is built on one form with a ḍummah on the final letter ( )or conjugated, i.e., the ḍummah or double ḍummah is due to the grammatical position of the word in the sentence ().
What is waqf with rawm? It is pronouncing a portion of the final short vowel, to be heard only by those close to the reciter.
It can be applied when the final letter of a word has a ḍummah or a kasrah, whether the word is built on one form ( )or conjugated

Complete: at the end of words that are not connected grammatically or in meaning to what follows them.
Iskaan: It is the omission of the final short vowel in pronunciation, replacing it with a sukūn. It applies to all diactitical marks.

What is the original form of these words in the Uthmaani orthography?

Joining words in writing is secondary to writing them separated which is the original form of words. It is obligatory to learn Qur’an recitation orally from expert reciters

It is obligatory to learn the recitation orally from expert reciters (i.e., teachers) who have mastered the recitation and who learned Tajweed orally from their teachers with an authentic chain of transmission back to the Prophet . It is not sufficient to read about Tajweed and study its rules if one is to recite the Qur’an properly. Learning about the places of articulation of the Arabic sounds and their manner of articulation from books is one thing and applying this knowledge is a different thing. It is, therefore, necessary to learn under expert reciters so that the student can hear firsthand the correct pronunciation of the Qur’an words.

This meaning is expressed in the following poetry verses: Whoever acquires the knowledge orally from a sheikh, Will be safe from diviation and altering the pronunciation of words. And whoever acquires the knowledge [only] from books, His knowledge, in the eyes of scholars, is absolute nothing.

These are the seven canonical reciters Their recitations are mutawaatir qira’aat by consensus. Today the majority of Muslims in the world, with the exception of some African and North African countries, recite the Noble Qurʾan according to the riwayah of Hafs on the authority of his teacher ‘Aasim of Kufa who was mentioned before. ‘Aasim received the Noble Qur’an from Abi-‘Abdur-Rahman ‘Abdullah ibn Habeeb As-Sulami and Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh who received it from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affaan, Ali ibn Abi-Ṭaalib, ‘Abdullah ibn Mas‘ūd, Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Zayd ibn Thaabit from the Prophet  from Jibreel  from Almighty Allah.
